full_judgment:
4. The present petitioner, as plaintiff, tiled Other Class Suit No. 109 of 1984 against the present opposite parties praying for declaration of title in the suit land. The opposite parties also filed Other Class Suit No. 22 of 1987 against the present petitioner in respect of the same suit land. The case of the present petitioner was that the suit land originally belonged to Giri Mistri who transferred the same to Madhu Kha the predecessor of the plaintiffs by registered kabala dated 29.02.1933. That Madhu Kha while in possession of the suit land transferred the same to Somir Mollah and Somir Gain by a registered kabuliat dated 07.09.1929 with an agreement that if Madhu Kha wanted to get back the suit land Somir Mollah and Somir Gain would reconvey the same in favour of him. According to that agreement Madhu Kha subsequently got the suit land reconvened from Somir Mollah and Somir Gain and started possessing that on payment, of rent regularly. Madhu Kha died leaving behind his four sons and two wives. Kosimon the second wife of Madhu Kha transferred her share to the defendant Nos. 5, 7; defendant No. 15 and plaintiff No. 6 transferred their shares to one Sajjad and defendant No. 13 transferred his share along with other share to one Mongal Khan the predecessor of the plaintiff Nos.  5 to 7 That the S.A. record was prepared in the name of plaintiff Nos. 1 to 3 But subsequently the plaintiffs, on receiving R.S. khatian, came to know for the first time that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in collusion with the recording employees recorded 11 annas share in plot Nos. 1229 and 1242 in their names although they have no title and possession in the suit plot. As the title of the plaintiff was clouded for this wrong R.S record, the present suit was filed. 

 5. The case of the contesting defendant Nos. 1, 2(Ka)-2 (Ga) who are the plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No. 22 of 1987, in short, is that Madhu Kha transferred 4.26 acres of land in favour of Somir Mollah and Somir Gain by kabuliat and patty dated 07.09.1929 and that there was no agreement for reconveyance of the suit land in between Madhu Kha and Somir Mollah and Somir Gain. That in S.A record the suit land was wrongly recorded in the names of the heirs of Madhu Kha and in R.S. khatian also some portion of the suit, land was wrongly recorded in the names of the heirs of Madhu Kha. That the plaintiffs-the heirs of Madhu Kha in fact have no right, title and possession in the suit land.
